verdict.rationale: Homebrew is a CLI you install and run on your own machines, with its source on GitHub. It installs packages locally into its own Cellar. Taps let you point it at any GitHub/git repository you control (`brew tap <user>/<repository>` clones it), so you can host your own formula and cask sources. One caveat: a user found hosting a tap harder than apt/yum because it needs a git server rather than a static file host. Missing for 10: documentation for mirroring or self-hosting the official core formulae, bottles and API; independent hands-on confirmation of a fully self-hosted setup.
